guidance.procedure: After deciding the relation, collect every complete responsive member: the operative sentence plus any governing lead-in, definition introduction, exception introduction, or continuation needed to express its force, actor, object, trigger, or scope. Include repeated provisions that independently resolve the hypothesis. Exclude headings, neighboring examples, generic security or duration language, and clauses that are merely useful context.

Identify an operative permission for the receiving party to disclose to recipients outside its organization. Consultants, advisers, contractors, agents, suppliers, affiliates, or other recipient-side representatives support only when the disclosure or access clause actually authorizes them. Employees, officers, directors, and internal researchers alone are not third parties; a definition bundling persons with a party or describing a signer’s status is not permission. Fixed filing offices, regulators, courts, or persons acting solely for the discloser do not by themselves establish recipient-side third-party sharing. Thus “employees may know; no other third party” opposes, while “employees and consultants may receive on need-to-know terms” supports. Include the governing permission or ban and any recipient definition supplying the authorized class.

Evaluate what may remain after the stated return or destruction is completed, independently of whether the duty is triggered by termination or request. An express archive, backup, legal-retention, dispute, or records exception supports possession. An exhaustive command covering all protected information and copies opposes it, as does “make or retain no copies” combined with final return, or alternatives requiring delivery of all and cessation of use versus destruction and deletion of all. A survival clause does not create retention permission. A duty limited to tangible documents or another subset is unresolved. Include the governing command and any carve-out.

Match the return or destruction duty to an ending event. Termination, expiration, project or service completion, ending discussions, abandoning a transaction, or the end of an evaluation period supports. A request-only duty is unresolved even if a separate clause discusses termination, survival, or agreement duration; do not import that event into the duty. Thus “upon request, return all” is unresolved, while “when discussions conclude, or upon request, return all” supports. Return alone suffices. Include the complete ending trigger and every return/destruction limb.

Separate survival of substantive duties from agreement duration and liability for past conduct. “These confidentiality duties survive termination” supports. A clause stating that the agreement and its obligations terminate at project completion or a fixed endpoint opposes survival when no substantive duty continues. A proviso that the recipient remains liable only for breaches committed before termination does not preserve the duties themselves; include the termination clause and endpoint limbs, not the antecedent-liability proviso alone. A fixed agreement term without either continuation or an express endpoint for the duties remains unresolved.

Inspect the complete operative definition and classify its subject matter, not its purpose or transmission mode. An exhaustive definition containing only technologies, engineering material, software, designs, specifications, know-how, or comparable technical matter supports; oral, visual, written, or tangible modes do not make it nontechnical. Express business, financial, commercial, personnel, customer, contractual, or marketing categories oppose. A generic “all information,” a blank or unspecified project or patent subject, and a technical-sounding purpose without defined content are unresolved. Use a recital only when it itself governs or defines the protected object; exclude neighboring background descriptions.

Ask whether identification is mandatory for every protected disclosure. A universal lead-in governing all protected information, followed by marking and oral identification-plus-confirmation procedures, supports; include the lead-in and all mode-specific limbs. An express alternative that protects information whether or not marked, by reasonable understanding, or because it is otherwise classified or considered nonpublic opposes universal identification, even if another branch covers designated information. Silence in a broad “any information” definition is unresolved, not opposition. Optional labeling, the discloser merely deeming information proprietary, or a classification scheme unconnected to every disclosure is unresolved.

Require an operative statement about conveyance mode. “Information transmitted verbally, in writing, or electronically,” when it defines the protected object, supports oral coverage, as do explicit oral, spoken, or verbal terms and comprehensive tangible/intangible formulations. References merely to discussions, information learned, agreement content, or information “in any form” within a subject-matter list do not establish verbal disclosure. If oral protection depends on designation or written confirmation, include the responsive condition sequence.

Require a specific independent-development provision, ordinarily stating development without use of, reference to, or access to protected information. A generic exclusions lead-in is responsive evidence only when paired with that particular limb. Public-domain, third-party-source, compelled-disclosure, nondisclosure, nonuse, or copying language alone neither permits nor prohibits independent development and leaves the issue unresolved. A direct ban on independent development would oppose the hypothesis.

Look for an incoming-source rule: information may be received, obtained, furnished, or acquired from a lawful third party not bound by confidentiality or other transmission restrictions. Pair the specific source limb with its governing exclusion introduction and stated conditions. A generic exception introduction, a legal-demand clause, an outgoing third-party disclosure rule, or an independent-development limb does not address acquisition and is unresolved. For example, “received from an unrestricted outside source” supports; “may disclose when compelled” does not.

Distinguish an affirmative copy allowance from a prohibition or handling rule. “May copy,” “make only the necessary number,” or “retain one archival or legal-counsel copy” supports permission for at least one copy. A clause stating “shall not make or retain copies without prior consent” opposes when the agreement supplies no operative copy exception; cite the full ban and continuation. A rule only preserving legends, forbidding obscured markings, or regulating storage leaves general permission unresolved. An exception governing a series such as “do not copy or disclose except as necessary” can authorize copying. Include the undertaking lead-in, and include a linked final-return clause when it supplies the scope of an expressly retained copy.

Require both legal compulsion and an operative warning duty. The trigger and notice may be in separate sentences: “disclosure is subject to law or legal process” followed by “promptly notify the discloser of that requirement” supports. Permission to comply with law, or a compelled-disclosure exclusion without notice, is unresolved rather than contradiction. Search beyond the exception list for a later notice sentence. Include the notice provision and the complete referenced trigger sequence; exclude unrelated exclusions or generic legal-disclosure permission that does not govern the notice.

Require operative authority for the receiving party to disclose or provide access to its employees. “May disclose to employees who need to know and are bound by confidence” supports, including when employees appear in a mixed list with consultants or advisers; include the undertaking lead-in and the employee exception. A signer merely being an employee, officer, agent, or consultant is status, not authority. A ban framed as “shall not disclose to any employee unless separately approved or separately made a party” opposes when the agreement itself grants no employee-sharing permission. Permission only for outside advisers is unresolved. Do not copy neighboring contractor, market-restriction, password, or security provisions unless they independently authorize employee access to the protected information.

Collect every provision that independently limits use to the stated purpose or forbids other use, including a governing purpose clause and repeated nonuse provisions. Exclude headings, disclosure/security duties, and a pure ownership or no-license clause. However, a construction clause stating that no license exists except a limited right to use solely for the stated purpose independently expresses the use limit and is responsive. After finding one restriction, scan the whole contract for a second operative restriction rather than stopping at the first candidate.

Support the hypothesis with an express denial of license, title, proprietary right, right of use, or other interest. A limited permission to review or use information for the stated purpose does not by itself oppose this no-proprietary-right proposition. Sole-and-exclusive ownership coupled with mandatory return can independently deny the recipient an interest; mere identification of the owner cannot. Include a linked construction lead-in and subordinate denial, and include each separate clause that independently denies rights.

Inspect whether the agreement, negotiations, contemplated project or transaction, or the fact that discussions are occurring is itself protected from announcement or disclosure. “Do not announce or disclose the project without consent,” protection of the agreement’s subject matter, and nondisclosure of negotiations or their status support the hypothesis. Confidentiality of exchanged business information, a generic entire-agreement clause, or discussion language describing purpose without protecting the discussions is unresolved. Include the operative announcement ban or the definition lead-in that makes the agreement, project, transaction, or negotiations protected; omit neighboring permissions about different facts.

Look for an operative prohibition on soliciting, recruiting, hiring, inducing departure, or otherwise approaching specified representatives of the disclosing party. A targeted no-contact or non-circumvention clause covering employees or other associated persons also supports the benchmark proposition when it forbids approaching them in connection with the contemplated transaction. General nondisclosure, noncompetition, or restrictions concerning customers or markets alone are unresolved. Include any lead-in supplying the actor, protected class, or duration.
